title: Export authored channel-strip volume automation
scope: Preserve Song.VolumeAutomations as GPIF channel-strip events with an explicit pinned-consumer loss report.
acceptance: Preserve two non-default values at different positions and their linear flags.
Preserve track ownership, per-track event order including equal positions, and exact GPIF values through Go reimport.
Independently prove that pinned AlphaTab ignores these events. Report each omission and require an explicit allowance for strict export.
exclusions: GP3 through GP5 beat-local mix-table volume changes belong to BeatEffects.MixTableChange; they are not evidence for the distinct Song.VolumeAutomations contract.

reproduction.instructions: Run ALPHATAB_CONFORMANCE=1 go test -count=1 -run "^(TestGP8|TestAlphaTab)VolumeConsumerLimits$" . The tests require exact wire/model preservation and scoped strict-policy reports for the independently observed consumer limits. Historical audit reproductions remain in evidence.

evidence.detail: The pinned GPIF automation dispatcher has cases only for Tempo, SyncPoint, Sound, and SustainPedal; it has no volume or DSPParam_12 case.
The pinned RSE channel-strip importer reads only the static Parameters child and ignores an Automations child.
The pinned GP5 importer converts a legacy mix-table volume byte into a beat-local AutomationType.Volume event, not a GPIF channel-strip Song.VolumeAutomations record.
Public contract; linked matrix cases are in obligation.

The proposed channel-strip volume export is still blocked by the required consumer, not complete implementation. Injected two DSPParam_12 ChannelStrip events at positions 0.25/0.75 with values 0.25/0.875 and different Linear flags. The public Go parser retains both; pinned AlphaTab reads zero volume automation events from the identical valid source archive. The original GP5 RSE.gp5 difference belongs to beat-local MixTableChange, not Song.VolumeAutomations.
